2608.00065.title: H+ Embedding: Harmonizing Global and Token-Level Retrieval with Context-Dependent Phrases
2608.00065.paper_summary: Terminology-intensive retrieval, especially in medical settings, depends on preserving multi-word entities, abbreviations, numerical constraints, and compositional concepts. However, existing representations lie at two extremes: single-vector retrievers often over-compress local relevance signals, while token-level late interaction retains every tokenizer subword at substantial indexing, storage, and scoring cost. This mismatch raises a natural question: can context-dependent phrases provide a useful retrieval unit between global vectors and tokens? We introduce H+ Embedding, a unified multi-granularity retriever that predicts variable-length phrase partitions, preserves uncovered tokens as singletons, and applies importance-guided unit selection with weighted MaxSim interaction. Across 16 scientific, medical, and bilingual tasks, its phrase retrieval branch exceeds the global retrieval branch by 6.91 macro nDCG@10. It also nearly matches Token while using 13.7% fewer document vectors and outperforms content-independent grouping rules under moderate vector budgets. Context-dependent phrase interaction therefore provides an intermediate quality-cost point between global compression and token-level interaction for practical retrieval systems.
2608.00065.paper_summary_zh: 術語密集的檢索，尤其是在醫療環境中，依賴於保留多詞實體、縮寫、數值限制和組合概念。<lb/>然而，現有的表示法存在兩個極端：單向量檢索器往往過度壓縮局部相關信號，而標記級的後期交互在指數、存儲和評分成本上保留了每個標記器的子詞。<lb/>這種不匹配引發了一個自然的問題：上下文依賴的短語能否在全局向量和標記之間提供有用的檢索單元？<lb/>我們介紹了 H+ 嵌入，一種統一的多粒度檢索器，能夠預測變長的短語劃分，將未涵蓋的標記保留為單例，並應用重要性引導的單元選擇，結合加權的 MaxSim 交互。<lb/>在 16 個科學、醫療和雙語任務中，其短語檢索分支超過了全局檢索分支 6.91 的宏觀 nDCG@10。<lb/>它在使用 13.7% 更少的文檔向量的同時，幾乎達到了 Token 的表現，並在中等向量預算下優於內容無關的分組規則。<lb/>因此，上下文依賴的短語交互為實用檢索系統提供了全局壓縮和標記級交互之間的中間質量成本點。
